subject: POC: Trial environment setup (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC)
messages:

Subject: POC follow-up & next steps — trial environment options (hosted/dedicated/VPC)

Hi Sofia / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC started: 

Success criteria (what RetailCo wants to validate):
- Throughput: sustained 30 concurrent reqs/sec at 256 tokens avg per request with p95 latency < 250ms for the main endpoint.
- Cost: target cost per 1k tokens against existing baseline (we'll instrument token-level cost).
- Feature parity: function calling and streaming must behave identically to your current setup for the checkout assistant.
- Security: data must be encrypted in transit and at rest, and logs must meet your retention policy (30 days).

Evaluation plan & timelines:
- Week 1 (this week): environment provisioning + smoke tests.
- Week 2: run representative workload (dataset + traffic replay) and measure latency/cost.
- Week 3: quality comparisons & integration checklist (function calling tests).

Ownership and roles:
- Redwood: Env provisioning, baseline perf runs, and instrumentation — Marissa (PM) + Dev (SE).
- RetailCo: Provide sample traffic traces, test accounts, and security contacts — Sofia/Tom.

Environment options we discussed:
1) Hosted sandbox (fastest): Redwood-managed hosted trial. Minimal setup on your side. Good for quick baseline and feature validation.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool): Predictable throughput and isolation; takes 2–3 business days to provision.
3) VPC/private trial (bring-your-network): Full VPC peering or private link for regulated data. Longer lead time (up to 2 weeks) due to networking + security approvals.

Immediate ask: can you confirm which environment you prefer to start with? If you want us to run baseline tests fast, we recommend hosted sandbox first, then upgrade to dedicated or VPC for final validation.

I've attached a short POC checklist and a network-config template to speed setup.

Next steps after you confirm environment choice: we’ll share an onboarding checklist and schedule a technical kickoff (30–45m) with Dev.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0138

Tom —

Great questions. Short answers below + attached doc with more detail.

1) Output consistency: we’ll include a quality regression check in Week 2 — side-by-side sampling on a fixed prompt set. If we see >5% deviation in your automated metrics we’ll surface quantization/kernel differences and recommend model variant or config changes.

2) Audit logs: for hosted sandbox we provide downloadable audit logs (JSON) for the trial window; for VPC/dedicated we can set up streaming to your SIEM (Syslog/S3 ingestion) — Dev will follow up on details.

3) Hosted sandbox default soft-limits for trials: 50 concurrent connections, 1M tokens/day; we can bump those for the POC upon request.

Proposed immediate plan (assuming hosted sandbox start):
- Fri (Week 0): RetailCo sends sample traces + test account credentials.
- Mon (Week 1): Redwood provisions hosted sandbox, baseline smoke tests.
- Wed–Fri (Week 1): traffic replay and perf capture.

Dev — can you confirm the audit log export format and the token-cost instrumentation we’ll surface? Also please advise if we need a firewall change for hosted sandbox (usually no) vs VPC (yes).

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: POC follow-up & next steps — audit logs / network notes

Hi all — quick technical notes: 

- Audit logs: hosted sandbox exports are JSON lines with fields: timestamp, request_id, user_id (if passed), model, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, and error_code. We'll provide a downloadable archive and an S3 export if you prefer.
- Token-cost instrumentation: Redwood will attach token-level cost breakdown per request in the perf reports; we'll surface aggregate cost per 1k tokens and a per-endpoint dashboard.
- Firewall / network: hosted sandbox — no inbound firewall changes required from RetailCo (we call out over TLS to the hosted endpoint). Dedicated/VPC — we'll need a CIDR and either VPC peering or private link. I've attached a network-config-template.xlsx for VPC steps and sample iptables rules.

For migration plan to VPC: allow ~10 business days for networking approvals and connectivity validation; if RetailCo has a procurement SLA that might add time.

Happy to run a 30-min technical kickoff next week to walk through the network template.

Regards,
